executive_assessment.text: UNICEF names district-level child vulnerabilities, while Sughd–Batken evidence highlights disputed water infrastructure and weak allocation institutions.
Migration/recruitment evidence is qualitative and indirect, not a causal or population-risk label. Named GBAO/Khatlon infrastructure and youth participation outputs add capacity detail.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026-07 reports: UNICEF rates 16 districts Very High and eight High for drought exposure; 918,108 children (26% nationally) face at least moderate drought. Temurmalik, Khuroson and Dangara are listed at 94%, 81% and 70% of their child populations, respectively.
UNICEF's district narrative identifies Rogun and Nurobod as especially exposed to landslide-related child vulnerability.

Source dated 2026-07 reports: UNICEF identifies high child-service vulnerability: Nurobod and Kuhistoni Mastchoh score 10.0 for WASH vulnerability, while Vakhsh, Qubodiyon and Tojikobod face education-service delivery challenges with scores of 8.1-8.7.
RUSI's 2025 targeted interviews and scoping synthesis describe rural farm-income and livelihood pressures, including in Khatlon, interacting with poverty, unemployment and migration decisions.

Source dated 2025-11-28 reports: RUSI reports that the STREAM programme in the Khojibakirgan watershed reportedly shows promise: women help identify water-management gaps and shape adaptation responses.
Source dated 2024-04-05 reports: The World Bank reports 17 bridges rehabilitated in GBAO, 27.5 km of embankments in Khatlon, and 20 road sections renovated, efforts benefiting 676,000 people.

Source dated 2024-04-05 reports: The Bank says its preventative resilience approach focused on GBAO and Khatlon, described as vulnerable to natural hazards and FCV, and included social cohesion, stronger local institutions, youth-inclusive services and livelihood support.

The Bank's April 2024 feature reports 53 community projects completed and 17 youth centres refurbished, alongside youth training/livelihood support. Female beneficiaries' participation in planning, decisions or monitoring reportedly rose from 0% to 56%.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 20 of 20 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The CCDR release provides national estimates but not the underlying model scenario or a subnational breakdown for GDP effects; the full report was not inspected.
The NDC characterizes gender and sectoral vulnerability and lists plans, but does not establish evaluated adaptation outcomes; RESILAND figures are reported outputs, not causal impacts.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
UNICEF's district model is a relative index; indicator dates and detailed methods are not specified in its narrative PDF.

No inspected source documents armed violence directly preventing a named climate adaptation project in Tajikistan; the observed reverse-direction evidence concerns disputed water infrastructure and local resource-management capacity.

RUSI's climate-migration-radicalisation chain is qualitative and indirect. The report notes migration is driven primarily by economic/social factors, most migrant interviewees did not identify climate change directly, and the proposed recruitment pathway is not a prevalence estimate.
World Bank sources describe reported outputs and an FCV-sensitive multi-risk program in GBAO/Khatlon, not measured climate-attributable resilience or a causal climate-FCV effect.
The World Bank poverty/climate chapter exceeded the web reader's content-size limit; the GCF and ADB pages returned 403, so no findings from those sources were used.
Main directly checked International Alert's April 2022 publication date and its emphasis on management/infrastructure, RUSI's scoping methods, and the World Bank participation denominator.
The UNICEF primary PDF was reported read by the collector but could not be independently reopened by coordinator; district percentages require methods/indicator-vintage checks at human approval.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
